analysis: The PR only changes documentation: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md head lines 451-488 add a 'Selected-model recovery' section describing ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift. No code, protocol, key, attestation or encryption behavior changes in the supplied evidence. I read the new text against the threat model. It describes a provider-local capacity tick that retries operator-selected models blocked by memory. It loads with allowEviction:false and may unload only idle, non-excluded, non-protected resident models, with LRU ordering, dwell/idle/lease rules and a per-victim recheck. This touches A-018 (serving availability) and T-029/T-016-style availability concerns. The described design bounds eviction churn and does not expand the coordinator wire contract, attestation (A-015/A-016), or prompt confidentiality (A-001). The doc states victims are evicted before the load's own checks, so a later non-memory failure still costs one attempt's evictions. That is a documented, bounded availability trade-off, not a regression I can show. Nothing here alters the T-041 prefix-cache posture, TB-012 hold handling, or TB-002 routing. Remaining unverified: the documented behavior is not checked against ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift, which was not supplied. A future code review should confirm that isProtectedFromRecoveryEviction and evictionExclusions honor add-on holds (TB-012/T-059) and Autopilot pins. I cannot confirm that from the supplied evidence, so I record it as an open integration question, not a finding.
